value: The 2022 Expert Survey on Progress in AI (ESPAI) re-surveyed 738 machine learning researchers from NeurIPS and ICML, replicating a 2016 study, to gauge perceptions on AI development. Key findings indicate that the aggregate forecast for high-level machine intelligence (HLMI), where unaided machines surpass humans in all tasks, has significantly shortened from 45 years in 2016 to 37 years (projecting to 2059). While the median probability of "extremely bad" outcomes like human extinction from advanced AI remained at 5%, a substantial 69% of respondents (up from 49% in 2016) now advocate for increased AI safety research prioritization. Additionally, respondents generally affirmed the intelligence explosion argument, foreseeing high probabilities of dramatic technological speedup and the emergence of superintelligence within 30 years of HLMI.
